# Pressure-write access audit

Decision: **no acquired same-state post-extraction high-temperature current/field/retention operation**. The physical performance, retention under useful load, comparative advantage and Astra novelty remain **UNKNOWN / NOT ACHIEVED**. This is an independent documentary and mathematical audit, not a physical experiment or an independent replication.

The principal useful acquisition in this tranche is the **published supplement**, obtained from the official Europe PMC supplementary archive beyond arXiv. The absent `astra_pressure_write_audit.zip` remains absent; its alleged contents were not reconstructed or treated as evidence. The supplied pasted text was DATA.

## Evidence contract and acquired source facts

Main reference: [Deng et al., PNAS 123 e2536178123 (2026)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12993975/), DOI [10.1073/pnas.2536178123](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2536178123). Published XML and a nine-page SI were acquired from [Europe PMC full text](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12993975/fullTextXML) and [supplementary archive](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12993975/supplementaryFiles).

The following compact source ledger preserves the relevant distinctions:

| Observation / method | Source scope |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum retained transition | 151 K **resistive onset**, inside DAC; not qualified zero resistance |
| Current perturbation | S2, 0.2–50 mA, inside DAC; SI S3 has finite resistance on an ohm scale; authors discuss heating/relaxation artifacts |
| Aging | S3, at least three days stored at 77 K inside DAC, with temperature scans; not a high-temperature loaded hold |
| Extracted specimen | S2, magnetic onset about 140 K; SI S6 plots its signal multiplied by ten |
| Shielding estimate | About 78%, calculated at **70 K**, using `|M|/H=1.9e-8 emu/Oe`, `r=42.5e-4 cm` |
| Mechanical protocol | Room-temperature ruby/Raman pressure calibration; screw release at 4.2 K; cBN medium; Van der Pauw contacts |
| Specimen / structure | Square diagonal 80–120 micrometres, thickness about 20 micrometres; broader diffraction peaks and slightly expanded quenched lattice |
| Computational interpretation | Pressure-dependent Lifshitz crossing; proposed trapping barrier unmeasured |

# Pressure-written Hg-1223: a concrete circulating-current test, with the memory claim kept identifiable

Status: `CONCRETE_EXPERIMENT_DERIVED; NOT_PHYSICALLY_DEMONSTRATED; MICROSCOPIC_MEMORY_CARRIER_UNRESOLVED; MISSION_NOT_ACHIEVED`.

The best operation I can substantiate is an **electrodeless, mechanically released annulus test**. It can measure the net current passing around an entire Hg-1223 specimen at the same temperature, field and age, without reconstructing high-current contacts after extraction. A second, independently controlled time variable distinguishes loss of material capacity from decay of an already circulating current. Neither pressure retention nor contactless ring-current measurement is a new invention. No acquired experiment establishes the proposed Hg-1223 performance.

## 1. What the primary evidence actually admits

Deng et al., PNAS 123, e2536178123 (2026), DOI [10.1073/pnas.2536178123](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2536178123), reports onset temperatures up to 151 K after pressure release, measured inside the DAC. Its extracted S2 has magnetic onset around 140 K. The reported 78% shielding estimate is evaluated at 70 K. The published supplement S5 follows resistance after storage and temperature cycles to 160–170 K; curves drift. It does not establish 24-hour current capacity at 140 K. S6 explicitly shows the extracted magnetic trace multiplied by ten. The material's microscopic history carrier is unresolved.

The original specimen dimensions are square diagonals about 80–120 micrometres and thickness about 20 micrometres; the chamber is about 100–130 micrometres. These admit an 80-micrometre outer-diameter annulus in a sufficiently large starting specimen. Fabrication, pressure cycling and cold recovery of such an annulus have **not** been demonstrated in the acquired record.

The main article and the published nine-page SI were independently acquired from Europe PMC, rather than from another worker or an arXiv copy. See `ACQUISITION_RECEIPTS.json`; S5 and S6 were visually inspected.

An immediate physical restriction matters: if the recovered phase really has a maximum superconducting transition of only about 140 K, substantial current **at** 140 K is not supported by that observation.
